source_span: we reduce our 12-month price target to $220 from $300, based on 22X P/E multiple (down from 30X previously) applied to our normalized EPS estimate of $10.00 (unchanged)
source_chain: Nvidia's 12-24 month backlog and defined product roadmap shield earnings power over the next 12-18 months, therefore leadership uncertainty falls on the P/E multiple instead of the EPS estimate, therefore Goldman cuts its target to $220 from $300 purely via multiple compression (30X to 22X) with EPS unchanged at $10.00; invalidation: holds until more clarity emerges on future leadership and business momentum (the Apple analogy — the market needs time to find the right multiple).
pulse_chain: Nvidia is sold out for two years (backlog), therefore losing Huang does not cut near-term profit, therefore the damage shows up in what investors pay per dollar of profit, not the profit itself — Goldman's cut to $220 from $300 is entirely a valuation cut (22x instead of 30x) with none from lower profit forecasts; invalidation: locked-in orders protect 2027 revenue and do nothing for the valuation until a permanent CEO is named.
why: The pulse reproduces Goldman's own sequence — backlog protects earnings, so the hit lands on the multiple not the EPS forecast — correctly attributed to Goldman with the same figures ($220/$300, 22x/30x) and the same leadership-clarity invalidation, just compressed and reworded.
